source_text: Randomized controlled trials conducted in South Africa, Kenya, and Uganda between 2005 and 2007 demonstrated that medical male circumcision reduces heterosexual HIV acquisition risk by 50-60% in men, prompting the World Health Organization to recommend voluntary medical male circumcision as part of combination HIV prevention strategies in high-prevalence regions of eastern and southern Africa. [78] [118]
